lessons.title: Planning offal processing and keeping it hygienic
lessons.html:
Processing offal into products

Processing offal means turning the passed red and rough offal into clean products that can be sold: cleaned tripe, trotters, heads, livers, hearts, kidneys, and casings for sausage. Good processing gives the abattoir extra income, so offal must be handled with the same care as meat.

Before you start

  • Check that all offal has been passed by the meat inspector. Unpassed or condemned offal must never enter the processing area.
  • Check that the equipment is clean: tables, trays, tripe washers, scalders, knives and hooks.
  • Check water temperature on the scalder and washer is as set by your supervisor.
  • Wear clean protective clothing: white overall, apron, hairnet, boots and gloves where required.

Hygiene rules during processing

  • Work from clean to dirty, never back. Cleaned products must not go back past unprocessed offal.
  • Keep red offal and rough offal processing apart.
  • Sterilise knives between tasks in the sterilizer.
  • Do not let products touch the floor or walls.
  • Wash your hands after breaks, after the toilet and after touching dirty items.

Why temperature matters

Germs grow quickly on warm, wet offal. The time between the slaughter floor and the chiller must be as short as possible. Products that wait on a table in a warm room spoil and can make customers sick. If processing slows down, tell your supervisor so products can go to the chiller first.

Records

Many abattoirs record the number or mass of each offal product per day and the time it went into the chiller. These records show the product was handled correctly and help trace any problem.

lessons.title: Processing steps for common offal products
lessons.html:
Processing steps for common products

Tripe (stomachs)

  1. Empty the stomach into the waste chute and rinse.
  2. Scald and wash in the tripe washer for the time and temperature set.
  3. Check that it is clean and free of food remains.
  4. Trim, cool in cold water and pack.

Trotters and heads

  1. Scald or singe to remove hair, as your abattoir does it.
  2. Scrape and wash until clean.
  3. Remove hooves or horns where instructed.
  4. Rinse, cool and pack.

Red offal

  1. Separate heart, liver, kidneys and lungs.
  2. Trim fat, blood vessels and any marked parts.
  3. Rinse if your procedure says so and drain.
  4. Pack on trays or in bags and chill quickly.

Casings (intestines)

  1. Strip out the contents.
  2. Wash inside and out.
  3. Scrape off the inner layers using the casing machine or by hand.
  4. Grade, salt and pack as instructed.

Packing and labelling

  • Use clean, food-safe containers or bags.
  • Label with product name, date and any batch number used by your abattoir.
  • Do not overfill crates; crushed products spoil faster.

Safety

  • Scalders and hot water burn. Keep lids closed and keep your hands out.
  • Lock out machines before cleaning or clearing a blockage.
  • Floors are wet. Wear boots with grip and clean spills.
  • Lift heavy crates with your legs, not your back, or use a trolley.

Key points

  • Process only offal passed by the meat inspector.
  • Work from clean to dirty and keep red and rough offal apart.
  • Keep the time to the chiller short.
  • Label products with name and date and keep records.
  • Lock out machines before cleaning them.
